bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
bill.officialSummary: Firearm Industry Non-Discrimination Act or the FIND Act This bill prohibits the federal government from entering into contracts with an entity that discriminates against firearm trade associations or businesses that deal in firearms, ammunition, or related products. Specifically, the bill requires a federal agency to include in each contract for the procurement of goods or services awarded by the agency a clause requiring the prime contractor to certify that it (1) has no policy, practice, guidance, or directive that discriminates against a firearm entity or firearm trade association; and (2) will not adopt a policy, practice, guidance, or directive that discriminates against a firearm entity or firearm trade association during the term of the contract. The bill establishes (1) a similar requirement with respect to subcontracts, and (2) penalties for violations. The bill makes such prohibition inapplicable to a contract for the procurement of goods or services that is a sole-source contract.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would ban the federal government from entering into contracts with an entity that discriminates against firearm trade associations or businesses that deal in firearms, ammunition, or related products.
plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in buying and owning a gun. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
